text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents original research with a primary focus on national-scale (China) future land use and land cover (LULC) prediction from 2010 to 2100. It implements eight distinct future scenarios combining Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) and Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs), enabling quantitative comparison across socioeconomic and emission policy dimensions. The study integrates the Global Change Assessment Model (GCAM) with the spatially explicit Future Land Use Simulation (FLUS) model to produce 1 km resolution LULC projections. It includes calibration of historical land use data, urban expansion modeling based on empirical socioeconomic drivers, and spatial downscaling with explicit geospatial outputs. Model performance is validated using quantitative accuracy metrics—kappa coefficient and Figure of Merit (FoM)—against observed CLUM data. All core inclusion criteria are met: national-scale implementation, primary LULC prediction focus, ≥2 future scenarios with comparison, spatial modeling with accuracy validation, and mapped LULC projections. None of the exclusion criteria apply, as the analysis is explicitly national, predictive, spatially explicit, and centered on LULC dynamics rather than being a methodological, economic, or ecological side study.)
